chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no extravagance regarding the meal.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on extravagance in food according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that 'israf' (extravagance/wastefulness) is not inherently present in food consumption itself, distinguishing the physical act of eating from the spiritual sin of waste. This hadith is often interpreted by Shia scholars to mean that while gluttony is discouraged, the mere quantity of food consumed does not constitute a religious violation unless it leads to neglect of duties or harm, thereby emphasizing intention and moderation over rigid quantitative limits.
